# Bumpers and tire carriers

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Trace bumper contours, cut and weld structural pieces with C-channels, then attach a swing arm assembly featuring multiple steel bars. [t1487]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Trace the inner contour of the bumper onto a steel plate to create mounting brackets.
2. Cut and grind all four mounting or structural pieces until they fit perfectly.
3. Weld each cut piece into place on the main bumper structure.
4. Insert a thirty-inch long C-channel between two structural brackets for strength.
5. Drill holes in the face of the bumper for hitch and clevis mounts.
6. Weld clevis mounts onto the structural pieces to secure them.
7. Attach the hitch assembly directly onto the C-channel section.
8. Cut slits into the end of the bumper to accommodate leaf spring shackle mounts.
9. Set the shackle mounts at a desired spacing from the bumper edge.
10. [Partial] Weld the shackle mounts securely onto their respective mounting brackets.
11. [Partial] Add small pieces of C-channel between shackle mounts for added strength if needed.
12. Attach additional gussets to the hitch area for reinforcement.
13. [Partial] Drill a one-inch hole in one end of a 3x2 steel bar for an attachment bolt.
14. [Partial] Tack weld a tire carrier hoop at a desired angle onto the swing arm base.
15. [Partial] Finish welding the entire swing arm assembly once the angle is satisfied.
16. Cut a pre-runner hoop in half to create horizontal supports on either side of the main hoop.
17. [Partial] Weld those support pieces flush with the backside of the main hoop at the same angle.
18. [Partial] Drill and cut a nine-inch piece of 2x2 steel tubing.
19. [Partial] Weld that nine-inch piece flush with the top rear edge of the swing arm hoop.
20. [Partial] Cut and prepare a fifteen-and-a-quarter inch piece of 2x2 steel tubing.
21. [Partial] Weld the longer 2x2 piece from the front of the swing arm up to the bottom of the previously welded nine-inch section.
22. [Partial] Drill six holes in a five-and-a-half-inch bolt pattern on a circular steel plate.
23. [Partial] Weld that drilled plate onto the top end of the nine-inch long 2x2 piece.
24. Add extra gussets to the center of one 2x2 member and the other holding the tire.

_Procedure reported by [t1487]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-diy-rear-bumper-and-tire-carrier.4139/>_

## Tools

- Grinder with cut-off wheels [t1487]
- [Partial] Welder (stick or MIG) [t1487]
- Drill press or high-speed drill [t1487]
- Circular file [t1487]
- Tape measure [t1487]

## Parts

- Circular plate: 3/8" thick steel, drilled with 6x5.5 bolt pattern [t1487]
- [Partial] Hi-Lift supports: Curved pieces of 1 3/4" tubing [t1487]
- [Partial] Hinge bolts: 3/4" long grade 8, with 2-3/4" ID bronze flange bearings [t1487]
- Main frame bar: 42" 3x2 steel, 1/4" wall [t1487]
- Support bars: 16" 2x2 steel, 1/4" wall [t1487]
- Swing arm hoop: 1 3/4" .120 wall, 18" tall [t1487]
- Wheel studs: M12x1.25 thread [t1487]

- **C-channel length**: 30" [t1487] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a brake press to bend the main steel plate if not bending by hand. [t1487]
- Tack weld swing arm pieces first before finishing welds to ensure correct angles. [t1487]
